question: Which part of the bifocal lens facilitates near vision?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lower part with convex lens**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **lower part with convex lens** in a bifocal lens facilitates near vision.
 
• Bifocal lenses are designed to correct both near and distant vision issues.
 
• The **upper part** of the bifocal lens is typically for **distance vision**, while the **lower part** is for **near vision**.
 
• This design allows individuals to see clearly at different distances without needing to switch between different pairs of glasses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bifocal lenses** were invented by Benjamin Franklin in the 18th century.
 
• They are particularly useful for people with presbyopia, a condition that affects near vision as people age.
 
• Modern variations include **progressive lenses**, which provide a gradient of varying lens powers for a smoother transition between near and far vision.
 
• Regular eye check-ups are essential to ensure that the prescription for bifocal lenses remains accurate.
